lifecycle.origin: Discovered and proven during MT-121 implementation on 2026-08-16; deferred to a new MT in the same WP per Operator directive so the finding is not lost.

scope.summary: HandshakeApp::refresh_mcp_snapshot builds a BRAND-NEW egui::Context for the model-vision capture pass. That fresh context has an EMPTY egui::Memory, so any surface whose open/closed state lives in egui::Memory is absent from the published MCP snapshot even when it is visibly open in the live window. app.rs already works around this for two surfaces by hand-copying the Reading-mode store and the open top-menu into the capture context, but pointer-opened PANE CONTEXT MENUS have no such projection. Consequence: a model driving Argus cannot see, target, or steer any context menu - it is invisible in argus.inspect while a human sees it on screen. This was proven live during MT-121 by tests/test_mcp_snapshot_viewport.rs::mt121_memory_backed_context_menu_remains_invisible_to_the_sized_capture_pass, which shows author_id 'ctx-menu.pane.pop_out' present in the rendered kittest frame and absent from the published snapshot. MT-121 fixed viewport SIZING only and deliberately did not fix this; the failing condition is asserted as current behaviour there, so that assertion MUST be inverted by this MT.

acceptance_criteria.text: A pane context menu that is open in the live window appears in the published MCP snapshot with its stable author_id, role and bounds, exactly as it appears in the rendered AccessKit tree.

The projection is general, not a hard-coded allowlist of one menu: any egui::Memory-backed surface the shell can open is projected into the capture context by a single documented mechanism, and adding a new menu does not require a new bespoke copy step.
Bounds published for the projected menu lie inside the declared SnapshotViewport and match the rendered frame, preserving the MT-121 coordinate contract.

The MT-121 test mt121_memory_backed_context_menu_remains_invisible_to_the_sized_capture_pass is inverted to assert the menu IS visible, and its comment is updated so it no longer documents the defect as expected behaviour.
A closed context menu is still absent from the snapshot: the fix must not make menus permanently visible, which would be a different falsehood.

proof_targets: PT-135-1: RED/GREEN of the inverted MT-121 assertion, both outputs captured verbatim.
PT-135-2: a mounted frame with a context menu open, OPENED and described, showing the menu present in both the rendered tree and the published snapshot with matching bounds.
PT-135-3: a negative proof that a CLOSED context menu does not appear in the snapshot.
PT-135-4: the full native lib suite still green (MT-121 baseline was 2069 passed / 0 failed).

target_entries: agent tool reference: which surfaces are visible to argus.inspect and which are not

risks: A blanket Memory copy could leak stale or half-open surfaces into the snapshot and make models act on a menu the operator already dismissed.
Copying Memory wholesale could import focus/scroll state that changes layout and breaks the MT-121 coordinate contract.
A per-menu allowlist would regress the moment a new menu is added, recreating this defect silently.
minimum_controls: AC-135-5 negative proof for the closed state.
